Fix a JusPrin bug: on a brand-new data folder, the Home page says "Your projects couldn't be loaded. JusPrin will keep trying." instead of showing the first-run screen ("Drop a model or project to start").

Repository: /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin, branch jusprin-newui (a fork of OrcaSlicer; fork code lives under src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/). Read AGENTS.md first, especially "Error handling discipline" and "Building on a shared machine" (check uptime and `pgrep -fl ninja` before building, use -j4, one build per build directory). Work in your own worktree, not in the main checkout.

What is already known (verified on macOS 2026-10-28):
- Home lists projects from <datadir>/jusprin/projects. That folder is only created when the first project version is saved (ProjectVersionStore.cpp, create_directories of versions/resources/...). The "Untitled" project JusPrin opens at startup writes nothing, so on a fresh data folder the projects folder does not exist.
- project_folders() in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp (around line 152) does:
      if (!std::filesystem::is_directory(root, error) && !error)
          return folders;
  It assumes is_directory() on a missing path leaves `error` clear. On macOS (libc++) it sets error to ENOENT "No such file or directory", so the early return never runs, the directory_iterator fails, the function logs "Local projects could not be listed: ...: No such file or directory" and returns std::nullopt. OrcaHomeBackend::recent_projects() (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp ~line 241) turns that nullopt into the "couldn't be loaded" message, and HomeHost keeps retrying once a second.
- A standalone check confirms the libc++ behavior: std::filesystem::is_directory("<missing path>", ec) returns false with ec.value()==2.
- The check came in with fork commit 1bc3ce84bb (2026-10-23, "Keep JusPrin up and visible when the projects folder can't be read or written"). No branch, worktree or PR has fixed it yet.
- project_folders() is also called from a second place in ProjectAutosave.cpp (around line 774); the fix must be right for both callers.

What to do:
1. Reproduce first, in the built app: launch with a fresh empty --datadir and confirm the error screen plus the repeating log line in <datadir>/log/debug_*.log. Existing build: build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <dir>.
2. Fix project_folders() so a projects folder that does not exist yet counts as zero projects (return an empty list), while every other error (permission denied, not a directory, I/O failure) still returns nullopt and is still logged. Do not swallow errors broadly; only the "does not exist" case is expected. Keep the change small and in fork code only.
3. Add a test that fails before the fix and passes after it: listing a missing projects root returns an empty list, not nullopt. Also keep (or add) coverage that an unreadable root still returns nullopt. Look at tests/workspace/real_adapter_harness.cpp (it already calls autosave.projects()) and tests/jusprin/test_home_host.cpp ("projects that could not be listed reach the page as a problem") to see where such a test fits. Show the test failing on the unfixed code before you apply the fix.
4. Verify end to end: rebuild, launch with a new empty --datadir, and confirm Home shows the first-run screen and the "could not be listed" line no longer appears in the log. Then create a project (New, add a model) and confirm it appears on Home after you return there.
5. The bug is a libc++/macOS behavior; say in your report whether you expect Windows (MSVC STL) and Linux (libstdc++) to behave the same, and label that as inference unless you tested it.

Do not commit or push unless asked. Report back: the cause as you confirmed it, the diff, the test that failed before and passes after (with output), and what you saw in the app before and after.

// The folders in the projects folder, or nothing when that folder exists but
// cannot be listed (its permissions, a storage fault): callers say so rather
// than treat it as holding no projects. No projects folder yet is a new
// installation with none.
std::optional<std::vector<std::filesystem::path>> project_folders(const std::filesystem::path& root)
{
    std::vector<std::filesystem::path> folders;
    std::error_code error;
    if (!std::filesystem::is_directory(root, error) && !error)
        return folders;
    std::filesystem::directory_iterator it(root, error);
    for (const std::filesystem::directory_iterator end; !error && it != end; it.increment(error))
        folders.push_back(it->path());
    if (error) {
        BOOST_LOG_TRIVIAL(error) << "Local projects could not be listed: " << root.string() << ": " << error.message();
        return std::nullopt;
    }
    return folders;
}

name: windows-build-machine
description: "Facts about the Windows Server 2022 machine used for JusPrin Windows verification (no admin, RDP at 100%, no GPU, toolchain and Mesa locations)"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 1e908987-3ebc-4e47-9372-ca2af82d4fee
  modified: 2026-10-23T15:13:22.028Z
---

The JusPrin Windows verification box (Windows Server 2022, user `guitest`, as of 2026-09-09): no admin rights, no GPU, reached over RDP at 100% scaling. VS 2022 Build Tools, CMake and Ninja are installed; the deps live at `C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local`. Main checkout `C:/src/JusPrin` is on `jusprin-newui` with a Release build in `C:/src/JusPrin/build`.

**Why:** Several handoff items were blocked on machine facts (no debugger, no admin, DPI cannot change from inside an RDP session), so knowing them up front saves a diagnostic pass.

**How to apply:**
- GL needs Mesa, and **every freshly configured CMake build tree starts without it** — nothing in CMake or the repo supplies it. Run `pwsh src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/windows-gl/provision-mesa-windows.ps1 -BuildDir <build dir> -Source C:\src\JusPrin\build\src\Release` after configuring; it copies `libgallium_wgl.dll` and `dxil.dll` (from `C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Redist\D3D\x64\`) beside every GUI exe and `opengl32.dll` into its `mesa\` subfolder. Placement is not interchangeable, and each missing file has a silent signature — both documented in "Software GL on Windows machines without a GPU" in `agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md` (on `jusprin-newui` since 2026-09-13, commit `318208608f`).
- Quick recall of the signatures: no `libgallium_wgl.dll` → `glcontext not ready, postpone init`, no `got opengl version`, black canvas all session. No `dxil.dll` → d3d12 initializes, then exit `0x80070057` on the first canvas draw with nothing logged. Both verified by removing the file and re-running. With all three present, both `d3d12` (default, `4.2 … D3D12`) and `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` (`4.6 … llvmpipe`) render.
- `slow_bootup` only moves the dxil crash from startup to first canvas paint; it is not a workaround.
- Lesson: a clear-only WGL smoke test passed under d3d12 because clearing compiles no shader, and was wrongly read as clearing the driver. A smoke test that skips the suspect code path proves nothing about it. (That test was removed from the repo for this reason.)
- A first-run datadir (e.g. copies of `C:\b\dd3`) logs ~630k lines in the first minute — the `GuideFrame::GetFilamentInfo` profile scan, driver-independent. Not a GL symptom.
- `D3D12 (Microsoft Basic Render Driver)` in the log is **Mesa's own d3d12 gallium driver on WARP**, not Microsoft's GLon12 mapping layer and not a real GPU. Confirm which GL is live by listing the process's loaded modules: the bundled Mesa shows `<exe dir>\mesa\opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` (+ `DXIL.dll` once d3d12 has drawn), the unprovisioned fallback shows only `C:\Windows\SYSTEM32\OPENGL32.dll`.
- The permission guard has refused `Remove-Item` under `C:\b` in some sessions (reported as a protected path) and misparses `rd /s /q` and path-like string literals as delete targets. On 2026-10-23, in bypass-permissions mode with the user asking for the delete, `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force` under `C:\b` worked. Build trees there contain a `src\Release\resources` junction into a worktree: list links first (`Get-ChildItem -Recurse -Attributes ReparsePoint`) and remove each with `[IO.Directory]::Delete(<link>)`, which deletes the link only, before any recursive delete.
- A debugger can be had without admin: download `https://aka.ms/windbg/download` (an .appinstaller pointing at a ~1.2 GB msixbundle), unzip the bundle, unzip `windbg_win-x64.msix`, and `amd64/cdb.exe` runs directly. Set `_NO_DEBUG_HEAP=1` when running the harness under cdb, or teardown crawls in the debug heap for many minutes.
- Fixture directories for the harness's visual modes must be short paths (e.g. `C:\Users\guitest\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\wp\...`); a long scratchpad path makes the profile-bundle copy exceed MAX_PATH and the fixture slice never validates.
- The harness prints everything on stderr; the exit code must be read with `$LASTEXITCODE` in PowerShell (bash shows 127).
- DPI at 150%/200% needs the user to reconnect the RDP session at that scale. See [[jusprin-windows-parity-handoff]].

Node is installed twice: the older `C:\tools\node` (v24.20.0), which is **not on PATH**, and
`C:\Users\guitest\.local\node-v24.21.0-win-x64` (v24.21.0, npm 11.19.0), added to the **user
PATH** on 2026-09-16. Check `Get-Command npm.cmd` before installing anything; a fresh Bash
session may still need `export PATH="$PATH:/c/Users/guitest/.local/node-v24.21.0-win-x64"`.

npm is not optional any more: since commit `5fc0efe2e3` the Agent and Home pages are built from
TypeScript and their `resources/jusprin/{agent,home}/index.html` is generated, not committed.
Without npm, CMake **fails at configure time** (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Web/CMakeLists.txt`
`FATAL_ERROR`), so the first new source file you add breaks the build tree; and without the
bundles the app creates no Agent WebView at all, which shows up as `shell_agent_webview_created
FAIL` / "the Agent page did not complete its handshake" in the shell harness. Build them with
`npm ci && npm run build` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI` and `HomeUI`.

The shell harness and the Agent page must come from the same commit: a harness exe built before
a page change hangs at `agent_reply_streams_to_completion` instead of failing.

To work on `jusprin-mcp` (the MCP stdio helper) you do **not** need an app build, and a worktree
can have its own build tree in about three minutes: configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF`
(skips the npm requirement above) plus
`-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local`, then
`cmake --build <dir> --config Release --target jusprin-mcp -- -m`, which compiles only the six
bridge/registry sources and `main.cpp`. `vswhere.exe` is **not** installed; vcvars is at
`C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\BuildTools\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvars64.bat`
and cmake at `C:\tools\cmake\bin\cmake.exe`. Point the Python suite at the result with
`JUSPRIN_TEST_BRIDGE=<dir>\src\Release\jusprin-mcp.exe`; the whole suite runs in ~8 s.

An **existing** build tree configured before node was installed keeps `JUSPRIN_NPM:FILEPATH=JUSPRIN_NPM-NOTFOUND`
in its CMakeCache, and `find_program` never retries a cached NOTFOUND -- so the next build fails at
configure with the `npm not found` FATAL_ERROR even once npm is on PATH. Reconfigure the tree once with
`cmake . -DJUSPRIN_NPM="C:/Users/guitest/.local/node-v24.21.0-win-x64/npm.cmd"`; putting node on PATH alone
is not enough. Neither the Bash tool nor a PowerShell session started before 2026-09-16 inherits the user
PATH entry, so prefix `$env:PATH` explicitly in each invocation.

**Shared build tree (2026-09-17):** other Claude sessions build and commit from `C:\src\JusPrin` and
`C:\src\JusPrin\build` concurrently. Do not patch that checkout or build there from a worktree session;
a link there holds `.lib` files and breaks their build (LNK1104). Use a separate tree instead: configure
with `-DBUILD_TESTS=ON -DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF -DSLIC3R_MSVC_PDB=OFF -DDEP_BUILD_DIR=C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build`
at a short path such as `C:\b\wsh`, which is a full `libslic3r_gui` build of about 40 minutes. To symbolize a crash
without a debugger, relink with a `ForceImportAfterCppTargets` props file (Link `GenerateDebugInformation`/`GenerateMapFile`),
read the fault offset from the event log (Application, event 1000), and run
`llvm-symbolizer --obj=<exe> --relative-address <offset>` (the symbolizer ships in the MSVC bin dir).

- The in-app browser pane renders a `file://` page as a static snapshot and refuses `screenshot`.
  To look at a rendered page (e.g. a vitest `PREVIEW_OUT` page), serve the directory over a
  throwaway node http server on 127.0.0.1 and navigate to that instead.

**Commits can hang in the `entire` hook (2026-09-25):** `git commit` from an agent session in a worktree
never returned; `entire hooks git prepare-commit-msg <file> message` alone hangs too (60 s, no output,
stdin closed). `--no-verify` does not skip prepare-commit-msg, and hooks must not be bypassed anyway, so
stop after one timed attempt (`timeout 90 git commit ... < /dev/null`), kill the orphaned `entire`
process it leaves behind (`ps -W | grep entire`), and ask Kenneth. Other sessions' commits carry an
`Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, so the hook works somewhere; the cause was not found.

**Concurrent harness runs collide on WebView2 (2026-09-25):** every harness exe uses the same WebView2
profile, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\JusPrin2\EBWebView`. While another session's harness is running (e.g. a
long `--home-printers-live` fixture run), a second harness fails at once with
`shell_agent_page_handshake_complete FAIL`, and its app log shows `JusPrin agent page failed to load:
The group or resource is not in the correct state`. That is not a page or bundle problem. Check for
`shell_integration_harness.exe` in `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process`, don't kill another session's
process, and set `$env:WEBVIEW2_USER_DATA_FOLDER='C:\b\<tree>-webview'` for your own runs.

**Scripting on this box (2026-10-06; Python corrected 2026-10-21):** no `python`/`py` on PATH, but Python 3.13 is at `C:\Users\guitest\.local\python-3.13.9\python.exe` and runs the prompt suites (`tests/project_prompt`, set `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` and `JUSPRIN_TOOL_CALL_CHECK`). Otherwise use node (`C:\Users\guitest\.local\node-v24.21.0-win-x64`). Bash heredocs and `node -e "..."` that contain backticks, `${...}` or backslashes get mangled by the shell; write the script to a file with the Write tool and run `node <file>`. The main checkout's build tree `C:\src\JusPrin\build` (VS generator, Release) is fine to build from a session that is working in the main checkout: `cmake --build C:\src\JusPrin\build --config Release --target <targets> -- -m` after `vcvars64.bat`; harness exes there read `resources\` from the source tree, so `npm run build` in `AgentUI` is enough to refresh the Agent page. A touched `Workspace.hpp` rebuild of `libslic3r_gui` + `shell_integration_harness` takes roughly 10 minutes.

Yes, I have what I need. The brief was written for your Mac, though, and this session is on the Windows box (`C:\src\JusPrin`), so a few things change:

**The bug happens on Windows too.** I tested this rather than guessing. I built a small test program with the MSVC compiler here. Calling `std::filesystem::is_directory()` on a missing folder returns false and also sets the error code, here to error 3, "The system cannot find the path specified." The early return in [ProjectAutosave.cpp:156](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:156) therefore never runs on Windows either, so I can reproduce and fix the bug here. For Linux I expect the same, since I believe libstdc++ reports a missing path the same way. That part is unverified.

**It affects how I write the fix.** Windows reports a missing folder as error 3 or error 2, depending on whether the parent folder exists, and the Mac reports it as error 2. A check against one exact number would therefore break on one platform. I'd test for "path not found" in a way that works on all three, so permission and other errors still return nullopt and still get logged.

**The function has two callers besides its definition**, at lines 784 and 865. The brief said "around 774"; I'll check that the fix is right for both.

- **Worktree:** under `.claude/worktrees/`. Other sessions build from the main checkout and its `build` folder, so I won't touch either.

- **Seeing Home:** screen capture is unreliable on this machine while the remote desktop session is disconnected. I'll confirm the first-run screen through the page's developer tools and the app log, plus a screenshot if capture works.

When the RDP session to the Windows verification box is **disconnected** (`query session` shows state `Disc` for the `guitest` session), `SetCursorPos`/`mouse_event` silently do nothing — `GetCursorPos` keeps returning 0,0 — and `Graphics.CopyFromScreen` throws "The handle is invalid". Only a *connected* session has an input desktop.

**Why:** This looks exactly like an application bug — gestures appear to have no effect and screenshots fail — so it can burn a long time before you realise the session, not the code, is the problem.

**How to apply:**
- Check `query session` first when input or capture stops working.
- Real UI testing still works without a desktop: `SendMessageTimeout` WM_LBUTTONDOWN / WM_MOUSEMOVE / WM_LBUTTONUP / WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK straight to the child HWND. This goes through the real wxMSW window procedure, real `SetCapture`, and real double-click handling — strictly more real than the harness's `ProcessEvent` injection, which bypasses `MSWWindowProc` entirely.
- A faithful drag must hold the pointer at a fixed **screen** x and recompute the client x from the target window's live `GetWindowRect` each step. Holding client x fixed makes a moving splitter run away, because the app converts with `ClientToScreen` against the window's current position.
- Screenshots still work disconnected through `PrintWindow(hwnd, hdc, 2)` (PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT): it draws the GL canvas and WebView2 panes (confirmed 2026-10-21). CopyFromScreen may not throw but returns a blank white image. But PrintWindow often returns the GL canvas as flat grey even at rest and after RedrawWindow (2026-10-22: grey in PrintWindow, tower drawn on screen). A grey canvas in a PrintWindow capture proves nothing; with a connected session, check with CopyFromScreen before calling it a bug or calling it fine.
- Read results from `EnumChildWindows` + `GetWindowRect` rather than pixels; assert that sibling columns tile the client rect exactly, which catches overlaps a per-window size check cannot see.
- P/Invoke `GetWindowTextW` must be declared `CharSet=CharSet.Unicode`, or the StringBuilder is marshalled as ANSI and the W call overruns the buffer and crashes PowerShell.
- The harness holds `shell_integration_harness.exe` open; kill it before relinking or the link fails with LNK1104.
- See [[windows-build-machine]] for the Mesa/GL and toolchain facts.

I built in its tree, `C:\b\pmf`, with 4 parallel jobs.

**Cause.** Windows behaves the same way as you saw on the Mac. `is_directory()` on the missing `jusprin\projects` folder reports an error ("The system cannot find the path specified"), so the "no folder yet means no projects" shortcut never ran. The folder listing then failed and returned nothing, and Home showed the error and retried every second. Before the fix, the log had 22 of these lines in the first 25 seconds:
```
[error] Local projects could not be listed: C:\b\pff-dd-before\jusprin\projects: The system cannot find the path specified.
```

**The fix.** It's one word in fork code, in [ProjectAutosave.cpp:156](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:156):
```diff
-    if (!std::filesystem::is_directory(root, error) && !error)
+    // exists() clears the error for a path that is not there; is_directory()
+    // reports it as an error.
+    if (!std::filesystem::exists(root, error) && !error)
         return folders;
```
- **Why `exists()`:** the C++ standard requires it to clear the error when the path isn't there, and it keeps any other error, such as permission denied. Those errors still fall through to the folder listing, which fails, logs the error and returns nothing, as before.
- **Side effect:** it also fixes a second case. A file sitting where the projects folder belongs used to count as zero projects with no error; now it's reported as unreadable.
- **Both callers covered:** `projects()` and `projects_for_source()` both go through this function, and the new check tests both.
